name: What is the difference between a toilet clog and a main drain clog?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a toilet clog and a main drain clog?

acceptedAnswer.text: A toilet clog is typically isolated to the toilet itself or its immediate P-trap, often caused by too much toilet paper or a foreign object. You might notice the toilet flushing slowly or not at all, but other drains in the house work fine. A main drain clog, however, affects multiple fixtures throughout your home, often causing water to back up into the lowest drains, such as a tub or shower, when you use a higher fixture like a toilet. This indicates a blockage further down the primary sewer line that serves your entire property.
acceptedAnswer.description: A toilet clog affects only the toilet, while a main drain clog impacts multiple fixtures, causing backups into low drains like a tub.
